questions.question: Name the three main kinds of components in an electric circuit, and explain what a switch does.
questions.expected_answer: A circuit has an energy source, such as a cell or battery; conducting wires that carry the electricity; and a device, such as a bulb, buzzer or motor, that changes electrical energy into light, sound or movement. Electricity flows only through a complete, unbroken loop. A switch opens or closes a gap in the circuit: when it is closed, the circuit is complete and the device works; when it is open, the circuit is broken and the device stops.

questions.question: What is the difference between a conductor and an insulator? Give two examples of each, and explain how insulators keep us safe.
questions.expected_answer: A conductor lets electricity flow through it, and an insulator does not. Most metals are conductors, such as copper and steel or aluminium. Most non-metals are insulators, such as plastic and rubber, or wood and glass. Insulators keep us safe because the plastic coat on wires, the plastic cases of plugs and the rubber handles on tools stop electricity from reaching our bodies.

questions.question: Describe how a coal-fired power station produces electricity, and give two ways to save electricity at home.
questions.expected_answer: Coal is burned in a furnace, and the heat boils water into high-pressure steam. The steam spins a turbine, and the turbine turns a generator, which produces electricity. The energy changes from chemical, to heat, to movement, to electrical energy. To save electricity, we can switch off lights and appliances when we are not using them, use LED bulbs, boil only the water we need, and take short showers.
